newsitem.title: HONG KONG: OAA chief dismayed at HK airport fee controversy.
newsitem.headline: OAA chief dismayed at HK airport fee controversy.

text.p: HONG KONG, Mar 24 (Reuter) The Director General of the Orient Airlines Association (OAA), Richard Stirland, flew into Hong Kong Monday to give a "severe warning" about the damaging effect high landing fees at the territory's new airport will have on airlines and the territory as a whole.
Stirland said the effect on freighters which operate on extremely tight margins could be especially dramatic forcing them to use cheaper airports nearby such as Macau or Zhuhai and Shenzhen in China.

In a speech to the Hong Kong Aerospace Forum, the head of the Manila-based OAA which represents 18 of Asia-Pacific's leading airlines, said he was dismayed at the proposed level of user charges at Chek Lap Kok and urged the Airport Authority to rethink its plans. He said the authority was relying on misleading comparisons to support its case for higher fees. Senior Airport Authority executives were in the audience.

"This is a severe warning to Hong Kong as a whole about the consequences of an ill thought out policy. The new airport has to be competitive. Charges at Chek Lap Kok should not be higher than at Kai Tak," Stirland said.
The OAA calculates landing charges for a Boeing 747-400 would be two and half times higher than at Kai Tak and at $8,754, Chek Lap Kok would be the world's third most expensive.

"The economics of operating all-freighter aircraft are extremely marginal and you either operate at 100 per cent load factor and make a very small profit or you make a loss - it's as simple as that. The pressure for freighters to operate into Shenzhen, Zhuhai or even Guangzhou and truck their cargo to Hong Kong is considerably increased by airport charges at Chek Lap Kok. One only has to look at the example of the number of airlines who switched their operations from London or Amsterdam to Maastricht," Stirland said.
He also said airlines would no longer find it profitable to operate transit flights into Hong Kong and potential new links would not be developed.

The most recent meeting earlier this month between the Airport Authority and airline representatives to discuss the controversial fee issue ended in disappointment and frustration, according to IATA representatives. The next meeting, the sixth in the series, is due next month. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+5017
